spans.s:
पोत पोत, अस्, m. (said to be fr. rt. 1. पू,
but probably fr. a lost rt. पु, ‘to beget’), the young
of any animal [cf. मृग-प्˚]; a colt, foal; a young
elephant ten years old; a young plant or tree, the young
shoot of a plant; a fetus which has no enveloping mem-
brane; cloth, a garment; the foundation of a house [cf.
पोट]; the site of a house or dwelling; (अस्, अम्), m.
n. a vessel, ship, boat; [cf. पुत्र, २. पुंस्; Gr. πῶλο-ς
for ποϝ-λο-ς, πωλ-ίο-ν, πά-ϊ(δ)ς for παϝ-ι(δ)ς,
πο-ία, πό-α, perhaps ποιέ-ω fr. a form ποιο as in παιδο-
ποιό-ς; Lat. pullu-s, Marci-por, pu-er for pov-er,
pu-era, pu-su-s, pusa, pū-pu-s, pū-pa, pūpilla,
pu-tu-s, pūbes, pum-ilu-s, pumil-io, prœ-pu-tiu-m,
pō-mu-m for pov-mu-m, pa-pav-er; Goth. fula (n),
fula = Old Germ. folo = Eng. foal; Lith. pauta-s,
‘an egg.’]
—पोत-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, produced or de-
veloped from a fetus which has no enveloping mem-
brane (said of elephants and certain other quadrupeds,
as opposed to men, cattle, &c., which are called
जरायु-ज).
—पोत-धारिन्, ई, m. a ship-owner,
master of a vessel.
—पोत-प्लव, अस्, m., Ved.
‘floating in a ship,’ a seaman, mariner.
—पोत-
बणिज्, क्, m. ‘ship-merchant,’ a voyaging merchant,
sea-faring trader.
—पोत-भङ्ग, अस्, m. shipwreck.
—पोत-रक्ष, अस्, m. ‘ship-governing,’ a large
paddle used for a rudder, the rudder of a boat.
—पोत-वाह, अस्, m. ‘boat-conductor,’ a rower,
boatman, steersman, one of the crew who keeps
watch at the mast-head.
—पोताच्छादन (˚त-
आच्˚), अम्, n. ‘cloth-covering,’ a tent.
—पोता-
धान (˚त-आध्˚), अम्, n. small fry, a shoal of
young fish.

पोतक, अस्, m. the young of any animal; a young
plant or tree (e. g. चूत-पोतक, a young mango-
tree); N. of a Nāga; the site or foundation of a
house [cf. गृह-प्˚]; (इका), f. a kind of vegetable,
Basella Lucida or Rubra; Anethum Sowa, = शत-
पुष्पा; (अकी), f. Basella Lucida or Rubra; a kind
of bird, Turdus Macrourus (= श्यामा).

पोतल, अस्, or अम्, m. or n. (?), N. of a sea-
port on the Indus (the Παράλα of the ancients);
N. of the residence of the Dalai Lama in Lhassa
(also called पोतरक).

पोताल पोताल, अस्, m., N. of a Brāhman;
a wrong reading for पोतल, p. 598, col. 3.

पोतलक, अस्, or अम्, m. or n. (?), N. of a moun-
tain (= पोतल?).
—पोतलक-प्रिय, अस्, m. ‘fond
of the mountain Potalaka,’ N. of a Buddha; of a
Jina or deified teacher of the Jainas.

पोतु, उस्, m. (fr. rt. 1. पू), = मानभाण्ड-
शोधक.

पोतृ, ता, m. ‘the purifier,’ an epithet of one of
the sixteen officiating priests (ऋत्व्-इज्) at a sacrifice,
the assistant of the Brahman, (Sāy. = पोतृ-नाम-
कर्त्विज् or यज्ञस्य शोधयितृ); an epithet of
Viṣṇu.
पोत्या, f. = पोतानां समूहः, see Gaṇa to Pāṇ.

पोत्र, अम्, n. the Soma vessel of the Potṛ, the
office of the Potṛ, (Sāy. = पोत्रा कृतं कर्म,
पोतुर् यज्ञः); a ship, boat [cf. पोत]; the
snout of a hog; a ploughshare; a dress, garment (?);
a thunderbolt (?).
—पोत्र-मण्डल, अम्, n. ‘snout-
orb,’ the round snout (of a hog &c.).
—पोत्रा-
युध (˚र-आय्˚), अस्, m. ‘armed with a snout,’ a
hog, boar.

पोत्रिन्, ई, m. a hog, boar.
—पोत्रि-दंष्ट्रा-ज,
अस्, m. ‘produced in the tusk of a boar,’ a kind of
gem supposed to be found in the tusk of a boar.
—पोत्रि-रथा, f. ‘hog-vehicled,’ (with Buddhists)
an epithet of Māyā; (with Jainas) N. of a Śakti or
female divinity.

पोत्रीय, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. relating or belonging to
the Potṛ.

पोतास पोतास, अस्, m. a species of camphor;
[cf. Eng. potash.]

पोतिमत्सक पोतिमत्सक, अस्, m., N. of a
prince.
